meta.title_plain: How topspin makes a tennis ball dive
meta.teaser: Why a spinning ball dips down: the air science behind big forehands.

page.title: How topspin makes a tennis ball dive like magic
page.bigIdea: A ball spinning forward pushes on the air, and the air pushes back. That is why topspin lets you hit high and still land it in.

cards.title: It starts with your swing
cards.front: Spin begins the moment strings touch the ball.
cards.back: You swing from low to high, up and forward. The racket face tilts slightly down. Your strings brush up the back of the ball, so it rolls forward.
cards.tryit: Shadow-swing 10 forehands slowly. Start below your knee and finish above your shoulder.

cards.title: The ball drags the air
cards.front: A spinning ball is not alone in the air.
cards.back: As it spins, the ball's fuzzy surface drags nearby air around with it. So the air flows differently on the top and the bottom.
cards.tryit: Stir water in a cup, then stop. Notice how the water keeps swirling for a while.

cards.title: Air pressure pushes down
cards.front: Why does the ball suddenly dip?
cards.back: On top, the spin moves against the air, so pressure rises. Underneath, the air moves faster and pressure drops. Higher pressure on top pushes the ball down.
cards.tryit: Hold a paper strip under your lip and blow over it. Faster air on top lifts it up!

cards.title: Clear the net, stay in
cards.front: Topspin gives you a safety zone.
cards.back: Because the ball drops faster, you can aim higher over the net and it still lands in. That bigger margin of error makes you more consistent.
cards.tryit: At practice, hit 10 forehands aiming a racket-length above the net. Count how many land in.

cards.title: Nadal's heavy forehand
cards.front: Rafa turned spin into a weapon.
cards.back: His forehand averaged about 3,200 spins per minute and peaked near 5,000. Sampras and Agassi hit around 1,800. It worked best on high-bouncing clay.
cards.tryit: Watch a Nadal forehand clip. Notice how high it clears the net before it dives.

quiz.hint: Think about where your racket starts and finishes on a big forehand.
quiz.why: Brushing up the back of the ball from low to high makes it roll forward.

quiz.q: Why does a topspin ball dip down?
opts: The air pushes harder on top
quiz.hint: Look at card 3. Where is the pressure higher?
quiz.why: Spin raises pressure on top and lowers it below, so the ball is pushed down.

quiz.q: How does topspin help you in a match?
opts: You can hit higher over the net safely
quiz.hint: What happens to a high shot that drops faster?
quiz.why: A ball that dives can clear the net high and still land in the court.

quiz.q: Who first studied this spinning-ball effect in experiments?
quiz.hint: The effect is named after him.
quiz.why: German scientist H.G. Magnus tested it in 1853, long before modern tennis.

page.think: In your next match, when would you use a high, heavy topspin ball instead of a flat, fast one? Picture one point where it would help you win.
